about:
Crego Metal Systems, operating as Crego Roofing of New Mexico, has been based in the North Valley of Albuquerque (Los Ranchos de Albuquerque) since its founding in 1980. The company is family-owned and operated, with Stephen and Brenda Gregg serving as primary contacts. It began as a local installer and manufacturer of metal roofing for both residential and commercial projects.

The firm fabricates cut-to-length metal roof panels, flashing, and trim on-site using UL-approved roll-forming lines. Its product range includes CMS, R-Panel, and standing-seam profiles, along with seamless and box gutters, plaster trims, and custom plasma-cut silhouettes. Most standard orders are ready for same-day pickup; larger orders typically ship within three days. The facility also produces custom copper designs and offers green roofing solutions.

Crego serves residential homeowners, commercial builders, and roofing contractors across New Mexico. Its panels and flashing have been tested to ANSI/SPRI/ES-1 standards, exceeding minimum wind-uplift requirements. Past projects span single-family homes, commercial buildings, and specialty installations requiring custom metalwork.

The company emphasizes its “Edge of Quality Roofing” standard, combining UL-certified manufacturing with a price-match guarantee. Family ownership and local production allow quick turnaround and direct communication with the fabrication team.

name: Crittco Cable & Fiber
old_description: Crittco Cable & Fiber was incorporated in May 2007. It was formed five years prior as a subsidiary of Crittco Construction. Matt Hale founded the company in 2002 with then partner Barry Brawner. Hale spent 20 years in the water and sewer business and Brawner spent 30 in the telecommunications industry. Together they built Crittco…
about:
Crittco Cable & Fiber is based in Jonesboro, Arkansas. The company traces its roots to 2002 when Matt Hale, a 20-year veteran of the water and sewer industry, partnered with Barry Brawner, who brought 30 years of telecommunications experience. They formed the business as a subsidiary of Crittco Construction and incorporated it in May 2007.

The firm operates as a full-service utility contractor with a focus on directional drilling. From an 8,000-square-foot shop supplemented by storage units and a covered wash bay, a crew of 12 to 30 runs a fleet that includes six drill rigs (ranging from a 7×11 to a 24×40), bucket trucks, backhoes, mini excavators, plows, vacuum excavators, bulldozers, and specialized equipment for duct washing and fiber blowing. Services span directional drilling, copper and fiber splicing, plowing, pulling and tugging, trenching and excavating, utility locating, aerial placement, duct washing, fiber blowing, and sewer, water, drainage, and electric installation.

Crittco serves telecommunications carriers such as Ritter Communications and AT&T, municipal utilities including City Water and Light in Jonesboro, and commercial contractors on projects for Hino Motors in Marion, Sam’s Wholesale in Jonesboro, Greene County Tech School in Paragould, and Home Depot in Jonesboro. The company also performed cable, fiber, and electric installation around new runways at Memphis International Airport.

The founders built the business on a reputation for high-quality work, on-time performance, and diversified project experience. Current leadership emphasizes evolving technology, quality workmanship, customer-oriented relationships, and a safe, efficient, environmentally friendly approach. The company describes its workforce as a family, with many employees remaining since the early years.

Production takes place in a 200,000-square-foot single-story facility on a ten-acre site in Elmhurst, supplemented by a 40,000-square-foot warehouse in California.

Crown Metal serves fashion retail, grocery, mass retail, brand, industry supplier, backroom, and domestic manufacturing segments. It counts five of the top ten U.S. retailers among its customers and supplies a broad cross-section of value-oriented retailers, high-end department stores, and overseas buyers.

about:
Custom Cable Corp., operating as Custom Wire & Cable, is headquartered in Westbury, New York. The company was founded in 1974 as a small Long Island distributor and has since grown into a global supplier of industrial wire and cable. Ownership details such as family, veteran, or woman-owned status are not publicly disclosed, and the founders are not named in available sources.

The company maintains an inventory of more than 15,000 active wire and cable variations, ranging from high-temperature wire and coaxial cable to multi-conductor and fiber optic products. Beyond distribution, Custom Cable provides value-added fabrication services including precision striping, twisting, paralleling, bundling, custom printing, dyeing, lashing, and the assembly of generator cable assemblies and fiber patch cords. Its capabilities also cover custom cable solutions, technical consulting, and quality compliance testing to standards such as UL, NEMA, ICEA, MIL, CSA, and VW-1.

Custom Cable serves manufacturers, contractors, OEMs, and distributors across a range of industries. Testimonials cite customers in manufacturing, aerospace, construction, electronics, and energy & utilities sectors. The company’s products and services support applications in factories, hospitals, data centers, and transportation systems worldwide.

The firm emphasizes a specification-driven approach rather than selling by description, highlighting its technical expertise, responsive service, and dependable turnaround times. Its team averages over 25 years of experience per sales professional, and the company positions its long-term customer relationships and rapid fulfillment — including emergency shipments and just-in-time programs — as core differentiators.

Custom Cut & Fab operates from Mandan, North Dakota, where its staff has been active in metal fabrication since 1992. The company began with a focus on HVAC fabrication and general construction trade work, building experience in evaluating drawings and resolving design issues before production.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication services, including HVAC fittings, galvanized and stainless steel components, copper countertops, and one-off special projects. Its equipment includes a 6‑by‑12‑foot waterjet capable of cutting materials up to seven inches thick and as thin as .002 inch, handling stone, marble, granite, plastics, foam, wood, and ceramics. A 5‑by‑10‑foot plasma table cuts metal up to 3/16 inch, primarily for HVAC ductwork and metal‑art pieces. The company can act as a subcontractor for large jobs or manage a project from initial design through final delivery.

Customers come from the HVAC, general construction, and metal‑arts sectors. Contractors seek the firm for ductwork and fitting fabrication, while designers and artists use its waterjet for decorative pieces in stone, metal, and other media. The company also serves clients needing custom countertops and miscellaneous fabricated assemblies.

The firm emphasizes its ability to review customer drawings, identify potential problems, and suggest work‑arounds, a capability developed over decades of trade experience. It also offers turnkey project packages that cover the full fabrication cycle.

Industrial work spans carbon steel, stainless steel, and aluminum, covering metal bending, custom fabrication, and projects ranging from prototype designs to facility renovations. Marine fabrication focuses on full-service top-side work for both commercial vessels and pleasure craft, including interior and exterior custom builds in the same three alloys. An in-house engineering team supports projects with CAD-driven design and drafting using AutoCAD, Rhino, Fusion 360, and SOLIDWORKS, offering surface modeling, solid modeling, piping design, and finite element analysis.

Customers come from industrial and marine sectors, including commercial ship operators and recreational boat owners seeking custom topside fabrication. The company does not publicly disclose specific client names or annual volumes.

CWT produces fine and ultra-fine wire components, including guidewires, coiled components, and Nitinol products. The company handles production runs from prototypes to large contract volumes, offering both bulk non-sterile and single-unit sterile assembly.

The company serves medical device OEMs ranging from large manufacturers to entrepreneurial startups. Its components are used in catheter accessories, cardiovascular valves, guidewires, and a variety of dental and surgical devices. CWT emphasizes manufacturing process validation and works with customers worldwide.

CWT highlights its consistent precision, high-quality repeatability, and implementation of the latest technology as key differentiators. The firm states that its management and production teams deliver unparalleled customer service, quality, and cost-effectiveness for specific medical device needs.

name: Custom Wood Artistry
old_description: Our handcrafted wooden products reflect generations of care, creativity, and hands-on skill. Founded by Troy and Sharon Foster, our family business brings together a love of woodworking, strong values, and a deep commitment to making every item count. Troy’s background as a proud Disabled Veteran of the United States Air Force adds another layer of dedication to everything we build. With help from children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren, we create custom wood gifts and keepsakes that feel deeply personal. Each handcrafted wooden product is made in the USA and shaped with patience, precision, and the kind of pride only a true family enterprise can offer.
about:
Custom Wood Artistry operates from Peever, South Dakota, where Troy and Sharon Foster founded the family-owned shop after Troy completed his service in the United States Air Force. A disabled veteran, Troy has spent a lifetime working with wood, from home building to custom pieces. The business is a multi-generational enterprise: the Fosters have been married for over 50 years and their six children, fourteen grandchildren, and two great-grandchildren all actively contribute to daily operations.

The company produces handcrafted wooden gifts, decor, and keepsakes entirely in the United States. Its catalog spans snack trays and serving boards, cribbage boards, lidded boxes with magnetic closures, plaques and wall signs, magnets, wood toys, and numismatic displays for coins and medallions. A dedicated wood engraving service adds personalized finishing touches. Products are shaped from a rotating selection of domestic and exotic hardwoods — including Sapele, Yellowheart, Wenge, Bubinga, Paduk, Purpleheart, Zebrawood, Lacewood, and Canary — with attention to grain, finish, and detail.

Customers range from individuals seeking personalized gifts for birthdays, military honors, or corporate thank-yous to restaurants and businesses ordering custom signs. The patriotic and military-themed line — featuring branch-specific lids, eagle boxes, and flag-inspired trays — serves veterans, active-duty families, and collectors. Numismatic trays and boxes cater to coin collectors. Nationwide shipping extends the shop's reach beyond its rural South Dakota location.

The Fosters frame the business around generational pride and the desire to turn meaningful moments into lasting keepsakes. Troy's military background is cited as a source of discipline and dedication that informs every build, while the family's collective involvement ensures each piece carries a personal touch that mass-produced alternatives cannot replicate.

about:
Colorado Springs Sawmill at Penrose operates from 240 3rd Street in Penrose, Colorado. The business is locally owned and operated, with craftsman Mitch the workshop. Founded on the principle of turning waste into value, the company's motto — 'from disaster to design' — reflects its start in repurposing dead and dying urban trees into usable lumber and finished goods.

The sawmill produces custom furniture, timber art, fireplace mantels, benches, chairs, and tables, often incorporating metal accents. Core processes include urban milling of local logs, kiln drying using a Nyle System high-performance dry kiln that cuts drying time dramatically, and wood-and-metal fabrication. The shop also sells imported live-edge slabs and offers kiln-drying services to other woodworkers. Facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not publicly disclosed.

Customers range from homeowners seeking one-of-a-kind pieces for homes, cabins, and campgrounds to municipal and commercial clients needing arborist and forestry services. The company's arborist division, A Noble Tree Company, provides ISA-certified tree care — including technical crane removals and pruning — across the Colorado Springs area. Urban milling services target property owners and municipalities looking for sustainable alternatives to chipping or hauling logs.

The operation distinguishes itself by offering a full chain from tree removal through kiln-dried lumber to finished furniture, all sourced locally. The Nyle kiln reduces wait times for furniture-grade slabs, while the ISA-certified arborist crew ensures professional tree care. The founder's emphasis on using 'everything we have right here where we are' underscores a hyper-local, waste-to-product model.

name: Custom Works Inc.
old_description: Full home remodeling services supported by custom woodworking and carpentry. From kitchens and bathrooms to staircases and mudrooms, we design and build spaces that are meant to last. Not rushed, not generic.
about:
Custom Works Inc. operates from Naperville, Illinois, where Serbian‑Macedonian founders Stefan and Melanie launched the business to blend Balkan woodworking heritage with Chicago‑area home remodeling. Stefan grew up in a small southern Serbian town learning carpentry alongside his grandfather, Dedo Stojan, while Melanie brought project‑management and interior‑design expertise. Together they built a husband‑and‑wife team focused on custom woodwork and full‑home renovations.

The shop delivers full‑service remodeling backed by in‑house woodworking: kitchens, bathrooms, staircases, mudrooms, built‑ins, vanities, custom furniture, and outdoor structures such as decks and patios. Projects follow a four‑step process — consultation, design, fabrication (typically 8‑10 weeks), and installation — with the team handling everything from flooring and fireplace updates to media walls and basement rebuilds.

Customers are residential owners across the Chicagoland suburbs. Recent work includes a basement flood restoration with a custom bar and media wall, a coffee table milled from a client’s own tree, a complete mudroom with built‑in storage, hardwood flooring throughout a home, and staircase and entertainment‑wall builds. The firm also tackles smaller jobs such as pantry shelving and bay‑window benches.

Custom Works positions itself against “fast furniture” by emphasizing pieces meant to last generations. The founders cite European‑rooted values — tradition, quality, integrity, sustainability — and pledge ethically sourced lumber. Clients repeatedly note transparent communication, realistic timelines, and a willingness to incorporate personal materials into one‑of‑a‑kind pieces.

about:
Cut & Dry Lumber Company operates in Albuquerque, New Mexico, where it launched an urban sawmill in 2018. The business is family-owned, building on more than 40 years of experience in the local tree-service industry. The founders, a family team that includes Lionel, began by refusing to send tree material to landfills, instead giving it away as chips and firewood before formalizing the upcycling operation.

The company produces live-edge slabs, custom-milled lumber, and made-to-order furnishings such as river tables, bar tops, benches, and desks. Its shop runs a Wood-Mizer LX 250 band mill capable of 54-inch-wide by 18-foot-long cuts, supplemented by a 24-inch planer, a 16-inch jointer, and a large sander for surfacing. All wood comes from Albuquerque’s urban forest—trees removed for instability, disease, or age—and is air-dried for up to two years in the desert climate before milling.

Customers include interior designers seeking custom furnishings, woodworkers and DIYers buying raw slabs, and clients needing contract shop work for milling or finishing. The company cites projects ranging from charcuterie boards and mantles to large conference tables, and notes that its contract milling service accepts logs sourced elsewhere.

The stated mission is to reduce green waste by giving a second life to Albuquerque’s trees and to build a tree-recycling culture in New Mexico. The owners frame the sawmill as a way to preserve the story of the urban forest in homes, shops, and gathering spaces.

about:
DAD Manufacturing, Inc. is headquartered in Hiawatha, Iowa, with a second high-volume facility in nearby Lisbon. The company was founded in 1980 by Dave Dohrmann, who remains owner and sales manager, and it operates as a family-owned business. From the start, DAD focused on solving a persistent problem in stainless steel fabrication: heat distortion during welding that caused warping and loss of dimensional accuracy. The founders developed proprietary welding processes and fixturing techniques to maintain shape and hold tight tolerances on large weldments.

The company specializes in stainless steel and aluminum fabrication and polishing. Core processes include laser cutting (tube and flat), bending, rolling, machining, TIG/MIG/spot welding, forming, and polishing to 2B cosmetic, #4 sanitary, and #8 aesthetic finishes. Powder coating and mechanical, electrical, or manual assembly are also offered in-house. DAD reports 2,632,781 parts fabricated, 217,348 jobs completed, and a 99% on-time delivery rate across 536 customers served. Its two Iowa plants together provide prototype, pre-production, and high-volume capacity.

DAD serves food manufacturing, pharmaceutical manufacturing, appliance and furniture, wind power, transportation, and government sectors. Long-standing customers include a pharmaceutical equipment manufacturer with a 36-year relationship and an ultrasonic tank manufacturer with a 21-year relationship. Specific projects cited include coating pan tanks for food and pharma, wedge wire baskets for the corn industry, custom aluminum ladders for wind power, and staircase railings for government facilities.

The company emphasizes its innovative welding and fixturing technology that enables statistically repeatable processes and tolerances of ±1 mm on weldments up to 10 feet long and 2,300 pounds. Hand polishing by experienced craftsmen achieves precise surface finishes. DAD attributes its differentiation to high quality, customer service, on-time delivery, consistency, tight tolerances, and family values cultivated over more than four decades.

old_description: The science behind Drake’s state-of-the-art injection molding operation assures exceptional quality and consistency in molded parts. When critical tolerances and other features are impractical or impossible to achieve with injection molding alone, we can deploy our precision machining capabilities to provide hybrid molded/machined part solutions to meet the specifications required.
about:
Drake Plastics Ltd. Co. operates from Cypress, Texas, where it was founded in March 1996 by Steve Quance. The company began when Quance, then an advanced products manager at a major stock-shape supplier, recognized that niche grades of Torlon® PAI were being neglected by large producers focused on high-volume output. A catalyst arrived when Atlantic Research Corporation needed glass-reinforced Torlon 5030 for the Javelin missile program and its existing supplier discontinued the product. Quance launched Drake to fill that gap, personally investing in specialized extrusion equipment and building a team around the technical demands of ultra high-performance polymers.

Today the company extrudes, injection molds, and precision machines a range of ultra high-performance polymers—including Torlon PAI, PEEK, Ryton R-4 PPS, AvaSpire PAEK, and Ultem PEI—into stock shapes, molded parts, and machined components. Its Cypress facility is described as the largest in the world dedicated to processing these materials, and it offers hybrid molded/machined solutions when tolerances exceed what molding alone can achieve. The operation also provides in-house CT inspection, CMM inspection, mechanical testing, re-curing, annealing, priming, coating, and laser engraving.

Drake serves aerospace and defense programs (notably the Javelin missile), OEMs, government agencies, universities, distributors, and fabricators worldwide. Sales offices in Germany, France, and Taiwan support global customers. The company’s stock shapes are supplied to machine shops globally, while its molded and machined parts go into applications such as electrical components, fluid handling, transportation, and oil and gas equipment.

The business was built on producing what larger suppliers could not or would not: niche grades in efficient sizes that minimize machining waste. Quance’s vision combined technical intuition with a commitment to long-term supply assurance, exemplified by the development of Drake 4200 PAI after Solvay discontinued Torlon 4200 resin. The company maintains AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015 certification and reports on-time delivery of 98% or better.

about:
The Durable Medical Equipment Re-Use Program operates from Cheltenham, Maryland, as a service of the Maryland Department of Aging. The state-run initiative provides free durable medical equipment to Maryland residents with any illness, injury, or disability, regardless of age or insurance status.

The program collects donated medical equipment, sanitizes and repairs it, then redistributes it through a network of distribution centers across Maryland. Equipment categories include basic items such as canes, walkers, shower chairs, and bedside commodes, as well as complex items like manual and power wheelchairs, power scooters, hospital beds, and mechanical lifts. All equipment is provided at no cost to the recipient.

The program serves Maryland residents of any age with illness, injury, or disability. It also works with healthcare professionals who complete applications for complex equipment, and partners with local organizations such as The Arc Northern Chesapeake Region, Delmarva Community Services, Queen Anne's County Department of Community Services, Cecil County Aging and Disability Services, Horizon Goodwill Industries, and Easter Seals to operate donation and distribution sites.

The program was established to improve quality of life by helping residents stay mobile, safe, and connected in their homes and communities. Its model removes financial barriers by providing equipment free of charge without prescription requirements for basic items, and without age or insurance restrictions.

The company works with clients across various sectors that require reliable transit protection, though specific industry verticals are not publicly listed.

The company emphasizes lower set-up and tooling costs compared to molded Styrofoam, along with the ability to adjust designs quickly and inexpensively as products evolve. Its team identifies the appropriate foam type, density, and thickness for each application, and the in-house water jet cutting capability supports rapid iteration without tooling delays.

about:
EightTwenty was founded in 2020 by Tony Capucille in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The company began as a vertically integrated solar developer aimed at serving Middle America, starting operations in Oklahoma in 2021 due to the state's high sunshine ranking but low solar adoption. Co-founder Kent Cissell joined as president, and the business is owned by employees and local investors in each market they serve.

The company designs and installs solar photovoltaic systems for residential, commercial, and tax-exempt customers, integrating battery storage and EV charging where needed. EightTwenty employs in-house craftsmen for installation and handles engineering, permitting, and project development across Oklahoma, Texas, Arkansas, Indiana, and Kentucky. The firm describes itself as a vertically integrated developer managing the full project lifecycle from utility bill analysis to system commissioning.

EightTwenty serves homeowners looking to hedge against rising electricity costs, commercial property owners and landlords leveraging tax incentives, tax-exempt institutions such as non-profits eligible for direct-pay credits, and builder partners seeking to incorporate solar, storage, and EV charging into new projects. Recent projects include installations for a brewery, a residential development, and individual homeowners across its service territory.

The company says its differentiation lies in a culture built on respect, focus, and quality, with a goal of turning every customer into a "raving fan." Leadership emphasizes that employee ownership and local investors align the business with community outcomes, and the Give Solar program directs a portion of each sale to help neighbors access clean energy.

With our bags, pouches, and labels, we offer a complete one-stop compostable packaging solution for sustainable business.
about:
Elevate Packaging is based in Chicago, Illinois. Founded in 2000 by Rich Cohen, a former corporate strategist and computer scientist at a Fortune 500 company, the business began after a 1999 sabbatical during which Cohen encountered tree-free papers made from invasive plant species. He launched the company to address the lack of viable compostable packaging alternatives.

The company develops and manufactures a full line of compostable packaging, including stand-up pouches (kraft, white, and transparent), flat pouches, cellophane bags, coffee bags, poly mailers, adhesive labels and stickers, packaging tape, and gloves. It offers custom design and full-color printing on compostable substrates, and operates a take-back program with the Compost Stewardship Institute to ensure used packaging is composted. The product catalog spans hundreds of SKUs sold in pack quantities of 100 units.

Elevate serves brands in natural and organic food, institutional food service, coffee and tea, cannabis, apparel, body care, e-commerce, and retail. Its solutions are used for product packaging, shipping supplies, and retail-ready packaging where compostability is required.

Cohen started the business after witnessing plastic pollution in remote wilderness areas. The company’s stated mission is to “Eliminate Plastic Waste and Create a Healthy Planet.” It differentiates itself through early commercialization of certified compostable pressure-sensitive labels (PURE Labels™), BPI-certified materials meeting ASTM D6400, and a circular-economy take-back service.

about:
Ellerbuilt Woodworks operates from Carson City, Nevada, where founder Brandon Eller established the shop as an extension of a lifelong dedication to woodworking. Eller’s path began with childhood projects — refinishing a bench at age ten — and deepened through study of Japanese joinery traditions. The business emerged from a philosophy that craftsmanship should reflect the maker’s full attention, not merely fill a space.

The shop produces custom cabinetry and handcrafted furniture for residential interiors. Offerings span kitchen and bathroom cabinets, built-in shelving and wall units, home-office desks and partner desks, bedroom pieces such as headboards and dressers, plus kitchen islands, bar cabinets, and entertainment centers. Work combines traditional hand-tool techniques with modern machinery, and finishes include conversion varnish, catalyzed lacquer, and UV-cured coatings. Wood selection ranges from domestic hardwoods — oak, maple, cherry, walnut — to softwoods like redwood and cedar and exotic species.

Clients are homeowners, designers, and builders seeking made-to-measure woodwork for kitchens, baths, offices, bedrooms, and entertainment areas. Each project starts with a site visit and design consultation, followed by a detailed timeline; smaller jobs may finish in weeks, while larger commissions can require several months.

Ellerbuilt distinguishes itself through an uncompromising standard: “If something is easy to do, it’s not worth doing.” Eller visits every installation space, designs for exact fit, and insists on joinery and finishing that will endure generations. The shop’s differentiator is not speed or volume but the deliberate, risk-accepting pursuit of pieces that carry the maker’s signature.

about:
Era Wire Inc. was founded in 1988 by Richard T. Rae in West Haven, Connecticut. The company began as a wire straightening and cutting service and used wire machinery dealer. After physical expansion, the operation moved to its current location at 19- in West Haven in 1995. Following Richard's passing in 2015, his son Rich Jr. assumed leadership, adding an on-site distribution warehouse and through-feed centerless grinding to create a one-stop shop for ferrous and non-ferrous wire needs.

The company specializes in precision wire straightening and cutting for round, flat, and shaped materials in all tempers and alloys. Its capabilities include through-feed centerless grinding as an alternative to turning and milling, heat treating, torsion straightening, and wire forming. A Quick Wire Program stocks pre-cut 304 spring-tempered stainless steel (including 304V and 316LVM), aluminum, copper, titanium, and high/low carbon steels for same-day shipping. The facility also provides wire machinery sales, parts, and tooling.

Era Wire serves the medical device industry as a primary focus, supplying precision-straightened Bright Diamond Drawn wire with zero surface marks for Swiss screw machining. Customers also include manufacturers requiring tight-tolerance wire for electronics and general industrial applications. The company's ISO 9001:2015 certification and compliance with RoHS III, REACH Annex XVII, and California Proposition 65 support regulated sectors.

The founder's original priority—servicing the customer first—remains the company's stated differentiator, summarized in the tagline "We give it to you straight." Era Wire emphasizes its ISO 9001 certification since 2004, same-day shipping on stocked items, and the ability to process difficult materials without surface damage as reasons customers choose them.

about:
F & P America Manufacturing Inc. operates from Troy, Ohio, where it was established in 1993 as a distribution and assembly facility. The company traces its roots to its Japanese parent, F-Tech, founded in 1947 in Saitama Prefecture as a metal toy maker. F-Tech began supplying motorcycle parts to Honda in 1959 and later became a tier-one automotive supplier. To support Honda’s North American operations, F-Tech opened a Canadian plant in 1986 and added the Ohio location as demand grew.

The Troy plant produces and assembles automotive components including pedal assemblies, front and rear subframes, and suspension parts. Core processes encompass progressive and traditional stamping of rolled steel, welding, hydroforming of steel tube, painting, and final assembly. The facility has doubled its building capacity twice, in 1996 and 2001, and today employs roughly 900 associates across 19 global locations under the F-Tech umbrella.

As a tier-one automotive systems supplier, F & P America serves major OEMs such as Honda, Toyota, and General Motors. Its parts are designed for direct installation on vehicle assembly lines, and the company also provides research and development support through F.tech R&D North America.

The company emphasizes a culture of quality and associate engagement, citing numerous awards for quality, delivery, safety, and community involvement. It holds IATF-16949 and ISO 14001 certifications and states that its workforce is central to delivering “unsurpassed quality.”

old_description: To support the growth of the food processing sector, the WMFPA in conjunction with the Community Foundation for Muskegon County (CFMC) and Muskegon Community College put in motion plans to develop the FARM (Food, Agriculture, Research, Manufacturing Center) accelerator and business development center targeted at stage one or two entrepreneurial companies or existing mature ones that are looking for an offsite location for test manufacturing of new products. about:
The FARM Food Processing Accelerator is located in Muskegon, Michigan. It was developed by the West Michigan Food Processing Association (WMFPA) in conjunction with the Community Foundation for Muskegon County and Muskegon Community College. A State of Michigan infrastructure grant of over $2 million awarded in 2019 enabled the project to move from plan to reality. Construction began in June 2020 and the facility was completed in early 2021.

The accelerator provides 8,000 square feet of flexible, food-grade manufacturing space designed for commercial fruit and vegetable processing. The facility meets USDA and FDA requirements and features loading docks, refrigeration and freezer storage, energy-efficient systems, and waste and water handling. Tenants supply their own processing equipment and occupy individual suites with flexible lease terms. The site also hosts the Michigan State University Mobile Processing Lab, which supports research, education, and workforce training.

FARM serves early-stage and growing food processing companies seeking a bridge from kitchen incubators to full commercialization. Target clients include entrepreneurial ventures at stage one or two, as well as established firms needing offsite test manufacturing. The center draws on partnerships with Michigan State University and Muskegon Community College to link students and researchers with industry projects.

The initiative was created to strengthen West Michigan's food processing sector by providing a dedicated scale-up facility, attracting venture capital, and integrating academic resources with commercial production. WMFPA technical experts also noted the facility's potential as essential infrastructure for emergency response, such as repackaging sanitizer during the COVID-19 pandemic.

The company designs and manufactures integrated voltage regulators that combine controller, FETs, inductor, and capacitors into a single package. Ferric holds over 40 patents built on a decade of research and offers product lines including the Fe1728 flexible multi-output converter, the Fe1736 16-phase buck converter, the Fe1766 ultra-high current density IVR, and the Fe1767 Newport dual-sided IVR for vertical power delivery.

Ferric serves AI and data center operators, high-performance computing customers, and mobile and consumer electronics manufacturers. Its IVRs have been proven in Apple products since 2021 and are targeted at hyperscaler environments where energy reduction is critical. The company's solutions scale across multiple power domains, supporting applications from AI accelerators to compact consumer devices.

Ferric states that its technology sets a new standard for current density, performance, and flexibility. The company emphasizes the highest current density in the industry (4.5 A/mm²), elimination of bulky discrete components with up to 74% component count reduction, and true vertical power delivery through dual-sided packaging. An ISO 9001:2015 certified quality management system underpins its commitment to continuous improvement and customer satisfaction.

Secondary services include pad printing, silk screening, hot stamping, flow painting, UV printing, CNC gluing and inserting, ultrasonic welding with IP67-rated assembly, and CNC finishing. old_description: Forever Fabrication specializes in custom automotive fabrication for performance vehicles and automotive enthusiasts. Typical work includes custom exhaust systems, turbocharger piping, mounting brackets, and other performance upgrades.
about:
Forever Fabrication & Welding Services is based in Lake Elmo, Minnesota. The company was founded in 2017 by Matthew Belz, who began welding professionally in 2014 while attending Hennepin Technical College. After gaining experience in motorsports fabrication, stainless and aluminum TIG welding, and production manufacturing, Belz started the business as a side venture creating metal art and custom automotive components. A collaboration on a catalytic converter protection system during a nationwide theft surge helped the business grow and reach customers nationwide.

The shop provides precision TIG and MIG welding on stainless steel, aluminum, and mild steel, handling brackets, assemblies, fixtures, and subassemblies from drawings, sketches, or existing parts. It also offers fabrication development with CAD layout and precise measurement, and coordinates laser cutting, CNC machining, bending, and powder coating as needed. Forever Fabrication specializes in small- to medium-batch runs and short-run production parts. In addition to contract fabrication, the company designs and manufactures its own performance exhaust components—including universal equalizer tubes, Helmholtz-style resonators, and turbo manifolds for the GM Vortec 4200 inline-six—developed through real-world testing.

The business serves two main customer groups. For B2B clients, it supports machine shops, product development firms, equipment manufacturers, and fabrication companies that need overflow capacity or specialized TIG welding. For automotive enthusiasts, it builds custom exhaust systems, turbocharger piping, mounting brackets, and other performance upgrades, primarily through referrals in the local performance community. A noted reference is B&H Machine Co., Inc., which has used the shop for multi-year fabrication and welding projects.

Founder Matthew Belz emphasizes strong customer relationships, clear communication, and dependable manufacturing support. The company positions itself as a streamlined, single-source solution with consistent quality, fast turnaround, and responsive service, combining technical welding expertise with practical problem solving.

name: GRK Manufacturing Co
old_description: GRK Manufacturing came into being in May of 1988 when Gary R. Kilday and family formed a corporation to purchase the assets of the Manual Arts Furniture Company. Manual Arts – or MAFCO as it was known – had a long history starting in 1915 as the only piano bench maker for the Baldwin Piano Company of downtown Cincinnati. Baldwin was a major provider of pianos in the United States and it turned to two “shop” teachers – manual arts teachers – to be their makers of piano benches. MAFCO provided Baldwin’s benches for almost 50 years.
about:
GRK Manufacturing is based in Hamilton, Ohio, and traces its roots to May 1988 when Gary R. Kilday and his family formed a corporation to acquire the assets of the Manual Arts Furniture Company (MAFCO). MAFCO had operated since 1915 as the exclusive piano bench supplier for the Baldwin Piano Company of Cincinnati, a relationship that lasted nearly 50 years.

Today the company runs a woodworking shop and a sewing division from its Hamilton facility, which it moved into in 1992 after negotiating with the Horn Lumber Company. The sewing operation has grown from a single part‑time seamstress to three full‑time staff, producing piano covers and bench cushions. The woodshop turns out a range of items including doors, retail and grocery store fixtures, mirror frames, and components for agricultural tripods, while also importing piano benches and dollies for music‑industry customers.

GRK serves the music, furniture, retail‑fixture, and agricultural‑equipment sectors. Historical customers include Baldwin Piano Company, the Nutone Company (mirror frames), and a North Carolina firm that bought solid‑oak tables. Current music‑industry clients receive both domestically made and imported benches and dollies.

The company emphasizes its willingness to take on new woodworking challenges and the steady expansion of its sewing capacity as key differentiators. The 2023 transition to former Operations Manager Rob Vicena marks a continuation of that adaptive approach.

The company differentiates itself through its breadth of inventory, mobile service convenience, and a service model that emphasizes personal customer support. about:
Generac Power Systems is headquartered in Waukesha, Wisconsin, where it was founded in 1959. The company began as the first to engineer affordable home standby generators and developed the first engine purpose‑built for generator use. No founder names or ownership structure (family, veteran, woman‑owned) are disclosed in public sources.

Today Generac manufactures the widest range of power products in the marketplace, spanning portable, residential, commercial, and industrial generators. It also designs and builds manual and fully automatic transfer switches for backup power applications up to 2 MW. The Generac Mobile line adds light towers, trailer‑mounted mobile generators, and combination units for demanding environments. The company pioneered the residential power washer category and now offers a full line of power washers, pressure washers, water pumps, solar battery storage systems, and smart home energy management platforms. Facility size, headcount, and annual production volumes are not publicly specified.

Generac serves homeowners through a network of authorized dealers, as well as commercial and industrial customers in sectors such as construction, mobile power, and renewable energy. Its products are used for home backup power, job‑site lighting and power, commercial facility backup, and off‑grid solar storage.

The company cites its early innovations — first affordable home standby generator, first dedicated generator engine — and its position as the #1 manufacturer of home backup generators as key differentiators. It also emphasizes the breadth of its product portfolio, leadership in transfer switches up to 2 MW, and a commitment to sustainability outlined in its 2025 Sustainability & Impact Report.

about:
George T. Hall Company (GTH) was founded in 1932 in Anaheim, California, by George Hall. For nearly a century the firm has operated under the motto "The House That Service Built." Today the business is led by Chairman Chuck Niemann and President Dina Johnson, with an executive team that includes a U.S. Navy veteran serving as technical manager in the Reno panel shop.

GTH manufactures custom UL‑certified control panels (UL 508A and UL 698A) in two dedicated panel shops located in California and Nevada. The company provides full‑service control solutions that span design, programming, instrumentation, control panel manufacturing, field services, system integration, and product distribution. As a CSIA‑certified system integrator since 2017, GTH modernizes legacy automation, delivers PLC and SCADA programming, and supports the full lifecycle of industrial control systems from commissioning through preventive maintenance.

The company serves public and private industrial customers across the western United States. Its industry portfolio includes water and wastewater, mining/minerals/metals, food and beverage, pharmaceutical and life sciences, general manufacturing, and aerospace. For mining projects GTH deploys MSHA‑ and BROWZ‑certified engineers; for food and beverage it applies ISA‑ and FDA‑aligned expertise; and for pharmaceutical clients it provides traceable PLC/SCADA systems that meet strict regulatory requirements.

GTH differentiates itself by combining panel fabrication, integration, field service, and distribution under one roof, reducing handoffs and accelerating project timelines. Its quality management system is certified to ISO 9001:2015 by DQS, and the firm emphasizes a culture of continuous improvement rooted in its founding service legacy. A recent white paper highlighted the ability to reuse up to 95 % of existing PLC code during SCADA migrations, preserving customer investment while lowering risk.

French emphasizes a full-circle process that honors each tree’s life, combining land preservation with craftsmanship. The shop’s integration of harvesting, milling, and building under one roof allows complete control over material quality and sustainability.

name: GlobalFoundries
old_description: GlobalFoundries operates the world's largest semiconductor fabrication plant in Malta, NY. Provides foundry manufacturing services for a variety of integrated circuits, serving customers in microelectronics, mobile, IoT and automotive markets.
about:
GlobalFoundries was founded in 2009 as a joint venture between Mubadala Investment Company and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) to address growing global demand for advanced semiconductors. The company established its global headquarters and flagship fabrication facility in Malta, New York, marking the first advanced foundry built in the United States in decades.

The company operates as a pure-play semiconductor foundry, offering a differentiated portfolio of process technologies including CMOS, FinFET, FDX™ FD-SOI, RF-SOI, SiGe, BCD, power GaN, and silicon photonics. Its manufacturing footprint spans five sites: Malta (NY), Burlington (VT), Dresden (Germany), Singapore, and Guangzhou (China). The Malta campus serves as a highly automated 300mm fab, while Burlington specializes in RF and GaN technologies. GlobalFoundries provides end-to-end services from wafer fabrication and bump (200mm/300mm) through advanced packaging (2.5D/3D, wafer-to-wafer, die-to-wafer), assembly, and test, supported by a vetted network of OSAT partners. Headcount ranges from 5,000 to 9,999 employees.

GlobalFoundries serves fabless semiconductor companies, integrated device manufacturers, and system houses across aerospace & defense, automotive, data center & communications infrastructure, home & industrial IoT, and smart mobile devices. Notable collaborations include a multi-year agreement with Marvell for high-performance SiGe optical connectivity, a partnership with TSMC to establish a U.S.-based source of silicon interposers for CoWoS® advanced packaging, and the acquisition of MIPS to strengthen processor IP capabilities.

The company positions itself as a differentiated technology partner that combines R&D, IP, design, custom silicon, and advanced manufacturing across a flexible global footprint. Its stated mission is to deliver "trusted, essential chips through deep customer co-innovation and partnerships," emphasizing supply chain resilience and manufacturing optionality for security-critical and high-growth markets.

old_description: Our GracePort and Grace Permanent Electrical Safety Devices (PESDs) drive innovation, enhance productivity and keep people safe and assets secure through simple and affordable solutions. about:
Grace Technologies is headquartered in Davenport, Iowa. The company traces its roots to 1993 when founder Phil Allen, while working on a friction welder retrofit at John Deere, identified a hazardous electrical access issue and launched Grace Engineering to develop the GracePort panel interface connector. The business evolved into Grace Engineered Products and was renamed Grace Technologies in 2020 to reflect its expanded portfolio. Leadership remains in the family: Phil Allen serves as Chairman of the Board, and his son Drew Allen is President and CEO.

Grace manufactures three core product lines: GracePort panel interface connectors that provide thru-door programming access to PLCs and control panels; GracePESDs, permanent electrical safety devices that combine presence-of-voltage LED indication with absence-of-voltage test points for lockout/tagout verification; and the GraceSense predictive maintenance system, IIoT smart sensors that continuously monitor vibration and temperature on switchgears, transformers, and rotating equipment. The company maintains roughly 16,000 active SKUs and ships orders worldwide within two to three business days through a distribution network spanning more than 60 countries.

Customers include industrial maintenance teams, electrical contractors, and original equipment manufacturers across sectors where incident energy exposure is a critical risk — such as manufacturing, power generation, and heavy industry. The devices are designed for low- to medium-voltage applications and are used to make maintenance safer, smarter, and more productive.

Grace emphasizes four differentiators: thought leadership in electrical safety, mass customization enabled by its large SKU count, fast global delivery, and a founding principle of being easy to do business with. Its stated mission is to pursue practical ways of keeping live voltage away from workers before, during, and after maintenance tasks, while empowering maintenance programs with IIoT sensor data.

name: Grand Rapids Chair Company
old_description: With approachable forms, customizable finishes, and built-in power ready to go, it keeps spaces looking fresh and working smarter. Solid wood or laminate, bold base or neutral tone—Clyde plays well with others.
about:
Grand Rapids Chair Company is based in Byron Center, Michigan, a suburb of Grand Rapids. The business traces its roots to 1991 when Dave and Jill Miller founded Manufacturer's Resource as a contract furniture sales company. Geoff assumed leadership in 2012 and today the company employs roughly 150 people.

The company manufactures commercial-grade seating and tables in its West Michigan factory. Production spans woodworking with solid hardwoods, metal fabrication in steel and aluminum, powder coating in more than 150 standard colors, and upholstery using high-performance textiles. An extensive fabric library and customizable finishes allow specifiers to tailor each piece. The factory's local footprint supports short lead times and the ability to fulfill one-off custom orders at volume-friendly pricing.

Grand Rapids Chair serves the restaurant, office, hospitality, and higher-education markets. Its product range includes chairs, stools, benches, lounge seating, communal and occasional tables, pedestal and T-base tables, and outdoor collections. Design partners and specifiers work with the company's in-house team and a network of independent industrial designers to outfit cafés, corporate hubs, hotel lobbies, and campus gathering spaces.

The Millers frame the business around a family mindset that values human connection. That philosophy extends to community involvement, such as the Brooke Chair—named for a family member with type 1 diabetes—which donates a portion of sales to the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation. The company says its differentiators are Michigan-made manufacturing, an warranty, deep customization capability, and a people-first culture that aims to make every project frictionless.

Its offerings include the Blazing Tubes system, conventional pump solar hot water systems, thermosyphon solar hot water systems, and residential photovoltaic systems that use only U.S.-manufactured components.

Grand Solar serves both residential and commercial customers across Hawaii. Its client base includes homeowners and businesses seeking solar thermal and photovoltaic installations, with the company positioning itself as a leader in the local solar thermal market.

name: Great American Packaging
old_description: Since 1966, we’ve delivered quality custom packaging solutions. We operate as a full-service packaging partner putting exceptional customer service at the forefront of everything we do.
about:
Founded in 1966 in Los Angeles, California, Great American Packaging has operated as a custom flexible packaging manufacturer for over five decades. The company produces poly bags, films, and specialty bags for food, ice, medical, and consumer applications.

Great American Packaging controls the entire production process in-house, from extrusion and printing to converting finished products. Its capabilities include custom extrusion, multi-color printing on state-of-the-art presses, and converting services such as bag making and film slitting. The facility is IFS PACsecure certified, meeting stringent food safety standards, and uses FDA- and USDA-approved materials.

The company serves industries including food processing, ice manufacturing, medical device packaging, and consumer goods. Its products are stocked by major retailers such as Costco and The Home Depot. Customers range from health and safety product manufacturers to food suppliers who rely on the company's food safety certified packaging and low lead times.

Great American Packaging differentiates itself through a 'white glove service' model that emphasizes consultative support, rapid turnaround, and reliability. The firm states that its commitment to controlling every production step allows it to deliver in ways other packaging companies cannot or will not, ensuring product integrity and on-shelf availability.

about:
Great Northern Metal Co. opened in November 2019 in Bozeman, Montana. The company was started by Rainor, a Gallatin Valley native, together with his brother and a group of friends. The team brought prior experience from multiple ventures and over 15 years in the metal roofing industry.

The firm operates as a metal roofing and siding supplier, providing panels, trim, and accessories for commercial, residential, and agricultural projects across a 500-mile radius around Bozeman. Its portfolio spans mountain lodges, commercial buildings, and farm structures. The company employs a production manager and an owner directly involved in production, suggesting in-house fabrication capabilities alongside distribution.

Customers include roofing contractors, architects, and building owners. Contractors such as Paramount Roofing LLC have cited precise orders, accurate lead times, and quality products. Architects value the supplier's input on panel profile, finish, color, and custom trim details during design phases.

Great Northern Metal Co. emphasizes a value-driven approach: honest information drawn from decades of industry experience, affordable pricing, reasonable timelines, and a relationship-focused model that extends beyond the initial order. The company positions itself as a knowledge resource for contractors navigating material options and project specifics.

Great Western Products operates from Hollywood in northeast Alabama, with a packaging hub in the Midwest Corn Belt. The company has been crafting concession foods for over 50 years, tracing its roots to popcorn production before expanding into a full line of fair and theater snacks.

The company emphasizes its low minimum quantity requirements for private-label programs, backed by long-standing vendor relationships and decades of experience in concession product development.
